recall_prompt: Say how you would answer this — give the definition in one line, and say what your example must show before it counts.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. The one line that earns it is R ⊆ A × B. Say which set comes first — a relation from A to B is not the same as a relation from B to A.
lines: Let A and B be two non-empty sets.
A relation R from A to B is any subset of the Cartesian product A × B.
If (a, b) ∈ R we write a R b and say a is related to b.
The set of all first entries in R is the domain of R, and the set of all second entries is the range of R.

recall.must_convey: That a relation from A to B is a subset of A × B.
accept: a relation from A to B is a subset of A cross B
any set of ordered pairs taken from A cross B
R is contained in A cross B
relation ante A cross B lo oka subset
pick some of the ordered pairs of the product

steps.why: Everything else about relations rests on this one line. Reflexive, symmetric and transitive are all conditions on which pairs the subset contains, so the subset statement has to come first.
steps.memory_tip: A relation is a chosen part of A × B — write the whole product, then keep some of the pairs.
common_mistakes: Saying a relation is a subset of A ∪ B instead of A × B.
Leaving out the direction, so it is not clear which set the first entries come from.
Describing a relation as a rule only, without saying it is a set of ordered pairs.

steps.label: Show a relation from A to B
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write A × B in full first, then point at the subset. That shows the relation was chosen from the product rather than written down from nothing.
lines: Any subset of this is a relation from A to B. For example:

lines.text: ∴ R = {(1, 3), (2, 4)} is a relation from A to B, with domain {1, 2} and range {3, 4}.

recall.must_convey: That A × B is written out and a subset of it is named as the relation, with its domain and range.
accept: write A cross B first then take a subset like one three and two four
any subset of the product is a relation
the domain is the first entries and the range is the second entries
modata A cross B rasi andulo subset theeskovali
R is one three and two four

steps.why: A relation is defined by being a subset, so the example is only complete when the product it sits inside is also on the page. Naming the domain and range shows the pairs have been read the right way round.
steps.memory_tip: Write the whole product first, then keep the pairs you want — those kept pairs are the relation.
common_mistakes: Giving a pair such as (3, 1), whose first entry is in B, so it is not in A × B at all.
Saying A × B is the only relation from A to B, when every subset of it is one.
Giving the domain as A when some element of A appears in no pair.
